title: T1055.008 — Process Injection - Ptrace System Calls
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Process Injection - Ptrace System Calls with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Teaching diagram of ptrace injection in 8 steps: an attacker logs in to a Linux build server with a stolen SSH key, enumerates processes, attaches to the ci-runner daemon (PID 2147, process identifier) with PTRACE_ATTACH, reads registers, writes shellcode into daemon memory, redirects RIP and detaches, then beacons to a C2 server. The SOC panel on the right collects auth, auditd, eBPF and network evidence at each step, and the final step shows defender containment.

steps.title: Login with a stolen key
steps.caption: The attacker logs in to the build server with a stolen SSH key that belongs to the ci-deploy service account. a service account logs in from an unusual IP address, outside the build window
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

fields.detail: The attacker logs in to the build server with a stolen SSH key that belongs to the ci-deploy service

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.caption: The attacker writes shellcode into daemon memory with PTRACE_POKEDATA or process_vm_writev . No file touches the disk. the eBPF sensor reports a cross-process memory write into the daemon

steps.title: Redirect and release
steps.caption: The attacker points RIP at the shellcode and detaches. The daemon resumes and now runs attacker code inside a trusted process. EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) flags execution from a memory region that no file backs
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.caption: Defenders verify kernel.yama.ptrace_scope , hunt older auditd events, isolate the host, stop the daemon, and rotate the exposed keys. containment in order - isolate, collect, clean, recover, rotate
